sources.note: Nothing stated. Tsuvan is cited on 11 pages (pp. 25, 37, 44, 136, 140, 142, 143, 154, 176, 206, 231) as cognate attestations copied from Brye's list with his tone diacritics, e.g. 'Tsuvan àbá' (leaf), 'Tsuvan və̀ɗέ' (night), 'Tsuvan fὲtέˀ' (sun), 'Tsuvan vwɔ́nέ' (rain), 'Tsuvan pərə-n to fly'; no sentence about Tsuvan tone, stress or accent occurs (regex over the full text: no match). Secondhand etymological database; confirms only that the sole tone-marked Tsuvan data in circulation are Brye's 120 words.

(unpublished word list).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing. Tsuvan (Johnston) forms are cited under 52 roots on 48 pages (e.g. dəgəva 'la panthère', dzədze 'grand-père', tʃəve 'la main', iɮe 'l'os', a gəlkən 'grandir'); a python census of all 52 cited forms finds no tone diacritic on any Tsuvan form (the only accented characters are in the French glosses). The foreword and classification pages contain no statement about tone or stress; the webonary HTML itself returns an automated-access block could not be reached by automated download. So the Johnston list, as transmitted by Gravina, is untoned, and the database says nothing about Tsuvan wor…

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: the reconstruction of the phonology and lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the linguistic history of the Central Chadic languages. LOT 375. Utrecht: LOT.
sources.note: Section 6.3.2 'Tsuvan' (p. 146) discusses only consonants and vowels, from an unpublished draft 'Vocabulaire mutsuvan' (Johnston n.d.): 'No firm conclusions can be reached about the vowel system without access to a detailed phonological analysis.' The whole reconstruction is stated to be 'not including tone or stress'. Nothing on Tsuvan stress.

sources.citation: Barreteau, Daniel & Michel Dieu. 2000 [online ed. 2005]. Linguistique. In Christian Seignobos & Olivier Iyébi-Mandjek (eds.), Atlas de la province Extrême-Nord Cameroun, 64-70 (planche 10). Paris: IRD Éditions & MINREST. OpenEdition Books full text.
sources.note: No phonology content. The chapter is a language inventory with lexicostatistic classification (nearest/farthest-neighbour dendrograms), vehicular-language and schooling maps. The whole Tsuvan entry (para 42) is: 'tsuvan : le tsuvan est parlé dans le massif de Téléki (est du canton de Tchévi), par le groupe connu sous le nom de Tchédé mais traité habituellement comme partie des Gude.' The words ton/tons/tonal/accent (prosodic sense)/syllabe do not occur anywhere in the chapter.
sources.venue: Atlas de la province Extrême-Nord Cameroun

sources.citation: Barreteau, Daniel, Évelyne Ngantchui & Terri Scruggs. 1993. Bibliographie des langues camerounaises. Paris: ORSTOM / ACCT. 274 pp. (PDF with text).
sources.note: Negative bibliographic evidence only: Tsuvan is listed in the classified inventory of Cameroonian languages (printed p. 223, p. 222) but the 'Index par langues' (printed p. 225 ff., txt from line 12615), which maps every language to the numbered entries of the c. 2,400-item bibliography, has no 'tsuvan' entry at all (the t- block runs.. tikar, tiv, tibea, to, tu'bora, tuki, tunen, tupuri; neighbours zizilivakan and gude are indexed, zizilivakan only to 0201 = Barreteau 1987). So as of 1993 the standard bibliography of Cameroonian languages recorded no work of any kind (phonologie, tonologie,…

sources.citation: Barreteau, Daniel (ed.). 1987. Langues et cultures dans le bassin du lac Tchad: journées d'études les 4 et 5 septembre 1984. Paris: ORSTOM (Collection Colloques et Séminaires). 218 pp. [esp. Barreteau, 'Un essai de classification lexico-statistique des langues de la famille tchadique parlées au Cameroun', 43-77; Barreteau, 'Du vocalisme en tchadique', 161-191; Wolff, 'Consonant-tone interference in Chadic..', 193-216]
sources.note: Only two comparative lexical items ('bouche' ma, 'oeil'-type item) and lexicostatistic percentages/tree position for tsuvan; no phonology. The volume's prosody discussions (Barreteau pp. 184-186 final-syllable 'accent d'intensité'; Wolff pp. 193-216 tonal accent) concern mofu-gudur, lamang, podoko, not tsuvan.

sources.citation: Barreteau, Daniel. 1987. Un essai de classification lexico-statistique des langues de la famille tchadique parlées au Cameroun. In D. Barreteau (ed.), Langues et cultures dans le bassin du lac Tchad: journées d'études les 4 et 5 septembre 1984, 43-77. Paris: ORSTOM (Colloques et Séminaires).
sources.note: Nothing on prosody. Tsuvan appears only (i) in the annexed comparative lists for 'bouche' (tsuvan : ma) and 'oeil' (tsuvan : adi(nə)) on printed pp. 61-62 (pp. 58-59), untoned like every other entry, (ii) in the MARGI-GBWATA dendrogram p. 69 (p. 66) and (iii) in the classified list p. 72 (p. 69). The words ton/tons/tonal/accent/syllabe do not occur anywhere in the chapter (pp. 43-77). Lexicostatistic classification from 120-word ALCAM lists; no phonology of any single language.
sources.venue: Langues et cultures dans le bassin du lac Tchad: journées d'études les 4 et 5 septembre 1984
